headline: Lights Flickering in Your House? What It Means in Sioux Falls
description: Lights flickering in your Sioux Falls house? Check bulbs, dimmers, and big loads in order, learn the winter causes, and know when to call (605) 250-4838.

mainEntity.name: Why are my lights flickering in just one room?

acceptedAnswer.text: A loose or failing bulb, a dimmer that doesn't match LED bulbs, or a worn switch is the usual cause. Swap the bulb first. If more than one light in the room flickers, a loose connection on that circuit is likely, and an electrician should test it.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal for lights to dim when the furnace or a space heater turns on?

acceptedAnswer.text: A short, small dip when a big motor or heater starts can be normal. A deep dim, flicker all over the house, or dimming that is getting worse is not. Move space heaters to their own circuit and have the circuit and panel checked.

mainEntity.name: Why are the lights flickering in my whole house?

acceptedAnswer.text: Flicker in every room often points to the panel, the meter, or the line from the utility. Ask a neighbor if they see it too. If they do, call your power company. If only your house has it, call an electrician, because a loose main connection can overheat.

One flickering bulb usually isn't. Flicker that comes with buzzing, a warm switch or cover plate, scorch marks, a burning smell, or lights that get brighter while others dim can mean a loose or arcing connection. Turn that light off and call an electrician.

mainEntity.name: Do LED bulbs flicker on old dimmer switches?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Many older dimmers were made for old-style bulbs and don't control LEDs smoothly, which causes flicker or buzzing at low settings. Use bulbs marked dimmable and a dimmer rated for LEDs. An electrician can swap the dimmer.
